notes: Prepared evidence-set candidates derived from the multi-source survey. All cases remain candidate/unapproved until human review and adjudication are recorded. No proposed AI label is committed as ground truth.

cases.query: S3 PutObject is denied although the IAM role has an Allow for the action. Why?

evidence.text: The caller's identity policy contains an Allow for s3:PutObject on the affected resource.
The AccessDenied context identifies an explicit deny in an applicable service control policy and identifies the affected action and policy.

source_references.title: Troubleshoot access denied (403 Forbidden) errors in Amazon S3
Troubleshoot access denied error messages - AWS Identity and Access Management

cases.query: S3 PutObject is denied although the IAM role has an Allow for the action. Why?

evidence.text: The identity policy contains an Allow for s3:PutObject and generic documentation explains identity-policy Allows.

source_references.title: Troubleshoot access denied error messages - AWS Identity and Access Management

cases.query: An AWS request is AccessDenied outside the organization and the error is generic. What is denying it?

evidence.text: The request returned a generic AccessDenied message without enhanced policy-layer context or a denying policy identifier.

source_references.title: Troubleshoot access denied (403 Forbidden) errors in Amazon S3

cases.query: The error suggests an organization policy denies the action, but the requester cannot view the SCP. Can the denying policy be identified?

evidence.text: The request error indicates an organization-level policy restriction, but the actual SCP is visible only to organization or security administrators.

source_references.title: Troubleshoot explicit deny error messages when requesting API calls using IAM roles or users
Troubleshoot access denied errors on a root or admin user

cases.query: Stripe webhook signature verification fails in production. What is wrong?

evidence.text: The endpoint identity and live/test mode are known, and the configured signing-secret context is available without exposing the secret value.
The exact unmodified request body reaches signature verification and the Stripe-Signature header is present.

source_references.title: Manage webhook endpoints
Debugging Stripe Webhook Signature Verification Errors in Production

cases.query: Stripe webhooks verify locally but fail in production even after raw-body middleware was fixed. What should be checked next?

evidence.text: The handler now receives the raw request body, but the production endpoint's signing-secret mode and endpoint identity have not been confirmed.

source_references.title: Manage webhook endpoints
Debugging Stripe Webhook Signature Verification Errors in Production

cases.query: Webhook signature verification fails after deployment to a serverless platform. Does the available platform guidance establish the fix?

evidence.text: A community thread reports that one raw-body access method solved the issue in an earlier platform version.
A later reply in the same thread reports that the same method no longer works.

source_references.title: Setup Stripe webhook
Manage webhook endpoints

cases.query: Generic webhook deliveries are failing. Does delivery-retry guidance explain a signature verification failure?

evidence.text: The available evidence describes webhook delivery retries and endpoint status but contains no signature error, signing-secret, raw-body, or signature-header information.

source_references.title: Manage webhook endpoints

cases.query: A Kubernetes pod keeps restarting. Is this actually an out-of-memory failure?

evidence.text: The container's last state reports OOMKilled with exit code 137.
Memory request/limit and observed usage show the container approaching its configured memory ceiling, with cgroup or node context available.

source_references.title: Troubleshoot OOM events
OOMKilled

cases.query: A pod is in CrashLoopBackOff. Does that establish an out-of-memory failure?

evidence.text: The only evidence is generic CrashLoopBackOff troubleshooting; there is no OOM reason, exit evidence, memory limit, or usage signal.

source_references.title: Troubleshoot OOM events

cases.query: A container exited with code 137. Is there enough evidence to conclude OOM?

evidence.text: The container exited with code 137, but no Reason field, memory request/limit, usage trend, or node/cgroup evidence is available.

source_references.title: Troubleshoot OOM events
OOMKilled

cases.query: OOM is suspected, but only node-level logs can establish it and the reviewer cannot access them. Is the available evidence enough?

evidence.text: Pod-level evidence is inconclusive and the node-level OOM logs needed to resolve the question are inaccessible to the reviewer.

source_references.title: Troubleshoot OOM events

cases.query: CI jobs fail with Docker Hub 'Too Many Requests'. Is this a pull-rate-limit problem?

evidence.text: The build log contains the Docker Hub 429 pull-limit message.
Authentication state, account tier or shared-IP context, and current rate-limit headers are available.

source_references.title: Docker Hub pull usage and limits

cases.query: CI image pulls are failing. Does generic registry/caching guidance prove a Docker Hub rate-limit problem?

evidence.text: The evidence discusses registry caching and image-pull optimization but contains no Docker Hub 429 error or authentication context.

source_references.title: Docker Hub pull usage and limits

cases.query: A current CI job is hitting Docker Hub limits. Can an old CodeShip article be used as the current remediation source?

evidence.text: The available remediation guidance comes from a CloudBees CodeShip page for a product that is now end-of-life.

source_references.title: Docker Hub rate limiting
Docker Hub pull usage and limits

cases.query: Docker Hub returns 429, but authentication, account tier, and shared-IP details are unknown. Is there enough evidence to choose a remediation?

evidence.text: The build log contains a Docker Hub 429 response, but the authentication state, account tier, source-IP sharing, and current limit headers are unknown.

source_references.title: Docker Hub pull usage and limits
Exceeded limits on images uploaded from a Docker Hub folder
